messages:
alice: heads-up — experimenting with a smoother eviction handshake for spot GPU nodes. goal: reduce cascade evictions when termination notices hit a node pool (esp mixed-capacity).
ben: curious — what does "smoother" mean here? longer drain window? rate-limited cordon?
alice: a few ideas combined: 1) extend preemption grace + stagger drain start times per availability zone, 2) add a transient node annotation so CA treats it as low-priority for scale-down for Xs, 3) pod-level fallback to cheaper instance-type pools via priority/toleration fallback policy.
carla: sounds promising. any perf/cost tradeoffs measured? we can't double GPU-hour cost.
alice: small sim so far: +15s median extra drain per node, ~3% fewer Pod restarts that triggered cross-pool cold starts. cost uplift negligible if we avoid full reprovisioning for hot warm-spare nodes.
dave: can you paste the proposed node annotation flow? thinking about k8s lifecycle hooks and the CA config we need to change.
alice: sure — rough sketch:

```
# when termination notice received
kubectl annotate node <node> redwood/eviction-window=extended:30s
kubectl taint node <node> preemptible=true:NoSchedule  # keep new pods off
# CA uses annotation to deprioritize immediate scale-down
```

Then per-pod: priorityClass + tolerations that let critical GPU tasks move to dedicated pool or fallback pool with toleration:

```
apiVersion: scheduling.k8s.io/v1
kind: PriorityClass
metadata:
  name: gpu-critical
value: 1000000
globalDefault: false
description: \"High priority for model-serving pods\"
```

and fallback policy (controller) watches for annotated nodes and proactively evicts non-critical pods with gracefulPeriod=60s to cheaper warm pool.

ben: this means we need a controller to implement fallback eviction and to rebind pods to fallback node groups? or rely on CA + node selectors?
alice: controller + evictor. CA reacts by scaling up fallback group if pending pods exist. controller moves pods by creating gated replacements (replica adjustments) rather than direct pod rebind. keeps things observable.

carla: could be risky for low-latency inference routes. How do we avoid evicting in-flight requests? any work on draining with in-flight-signal?
dave: we discussed SDK-level in-flight hinting: runtime emits a preemptible-suspend hook to load-balance new requests away for N seconds while draining. combined with read-only KV cache flush to preserve warm state.

infra-bot: alert: 2026-02-11T14:02:15Z — recent spike in GPU eviction counts in us-west2 (30m window). nodes affected: g4-*, preemptible.

ben: that alert lines up with the sim window. If we can avoid mass resecheduling, latency for tail requests should improve. need a small canary: enable in one AZ and measure 99.9th p99.9 tail.

alice: agreed. plan: implement controller, enable only on pool-gpu-spot-us-west2-a, set extended window 30s, pod fallback threshold 2m. collect metrics: pod-restarts, cross-pool cold-starts, p99 latency, GPU-hour usage.

carla: what about CA flags? we should set cluster-autoscaler expander to least-wasteful and add new prioritizer to avoid aggressive scale-down of nodes with annotation. also increase max-empty-bulk deletion threshold temporarily.
dave: patch idea for CA config: add a scale-down delay when nodes have `redwood/eviction-window` anno. pseudo:

```
scaleDownDelayAfterAdd: 10m
unneededTime: 10m
# custom: skipScaleDownIfAnnotation: redwood/eviction-window
```

we'll have to fork or submit an upstream CA PR for that custom field, otherwise run a small shim controller to re-label nodes as protected.

ben: how about fallback scheduling to cheaper instance types — we need to ensure model weights load times don't kill QoS. maybe pre-warm a small percentage of fallback pool with shared cache mounts.
alice: yep, pre-warm strategy: keep 5% warm spare with NVCache mounted, image pre-pulled, and model weights loaded into disk cache. controller will route evicted pods to those first.

carla: ok. checklist for canary:
- impl controller (evictor + annotation watcher) — dave + alice
- prepare fallback pool with pre-warm images — infra team
- CA shim to protect annotated nodes or upstream PR — ben
- instrumentation dashboards and alerting — carla
- run canary in us-west2-a for 24h, compare metrics vs control AZ

dave: I'll start a branch with controller skeleton and a simple reconciler that annotates protected nodes and evicts non-critical pods with `kubectl evict --grace-period=60`. will include feature-flag for dry-run.

alice: thanks — include a small synthetic load generator to validate in-flight suspend works.

ben: one more ask — add cost delta estimate to PR so PMs can sign off: expected cost change <2% if fallback ratio < 10%.

infra-bot: info: canary feature flag created: feature/spot-fallback-canary — owners: @alice, @dave

carla: stamping this plan. if any of the metrics show >5% increase in cold-starts or >2x tail latency, rollback immediately. :warning:

alice: noted. I'll post a short postmortem template for the canary run and we'll keep it under 24h initial window.

ben: cool. ping when branch ready, I'll set up the CA shim experiment.
